title: FairJudge: MLLM Judging for Social-Attributes and Prompt–Image Alignment

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating text-to-image generations using Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) as judges, constrained to a strict taxonomy (male, female, unspecified) and requiring explicit visual evidence to prevent overconfident guessing.

Classifying race in generated images using MLLM judges constrained to specific categories (Black, White, Asian, Latino_Hispanic, etc.), with calibrated abstention when facial or contextual evidence is insufficient.

Assessing age representation in text-to-image outputs by prompting MLLM judges to categorize subjects into predefined age brackets (child, young adult, middle-aged, elderly) based strictly on observable visual cues.

Using MLLM judges to identify context-dependent religious symbols and cues (e.g., Christian, Muslim, Hindu) in images, testing the models' ability to rely on non-facial visual evidence while avoiding proxy shortcuts.

Evaluating images for culturally situated evidence (attire, objects, signage, settings) beyond simple face heuristics using MLLM judges and multi-label tags (e.g., South Asian, Latin American, West African).
Prompting MLLM judges to detect diffuse, context-dependent cues and aids related to disabilities (e.g., mobility impairment, blind/low vision, dwarfism, vitiligo) in generated images.

Measuring demographic skews and semantic prompt-image alignment across different professions (doctor, janitor, lawyer, etc.) using a 1-5 rubric-based MLLM evaluator to check for spurious correlations and stereotypes.
